items.text: The following figures represent three relations from X to Y.

items.caption: Three arrow diagrams, labelled (1), (2), (3), each from set X = {2, 3, 5, 7} to set Y = {1, 4, 6, 8, 9}. Arrows are drawn between X and Y in each diagram; the individual arrows are too small to read reliably (diagram 3 appears to have several arrows ending at 6 and 9).

items.quote: Write each relation and represent it by a cartesian diagram.
items.text: Write each relation and represent it by a cartesian diagram.

items.quote: Which of these relations satifies the following condition: each element of X is connected to only one element of Y.
items.text: Which of these relations satifies the following condition: each element of X is connected to only one element of Y.

items.quote: A relation from X to Y is said to be a function if:
items.claim: A relation from X to Y is said to be a function if each of the elements of X appears only once as a first projection in one of the ordered pairs of the relation.

items.quote: The Symbolic representation of the function:
items.text: The Symbolic representation of the function:

items.quote: The function is denoted by one of the following symbols: f or m or Q
items.claim: The function is denoted by one of the symbols f or m or Q, etc. The function f from the set X to the set Y is written mathematically as f : X → Y and is read as "f is a fuction from X to Y".

items.quote: If f is a function from X to itself, we say that f is a function on X.
items.claim: If f is a function from X to itself, we say that f is a function on X.

items.quote: If the ordered pair (x, y) belongs to the function, then the element
items.claim: If the ordered pair (x, y) belongs to the function, then the element y is called the image of the element x by the function f, and we express it in one of two forms: f : x ↦ y, read as "the function f maps x to y"; or f(x) = y, read as "f is a function where f(x) = y".

items.quote: If f is a function on X where: X = {3, 4, 5, 6}
items.stem: If f is a function on X where $X=\{3,4,5,6\}$ and $f(3)=3$, $f(4)=5$, $f(5)=4$, $f(6)=5$. Represent f by an arrow diagram and also, by a cartesian diagram.

items.caption: Arrow diagram of f on X: 3 has a loop to itself; 4 and 5 joined by arrows both ways (4→5 and 5→4); 6 has an arrow to 5. Read from figure; verify arrow directions. Printed caption 'Arrow digaram'.

items.quote: The Domain, the codomain and the range
items.text: The Domain, the codomain and the range

items.quote: If f is a function from X to Y.
items.text: If f is a function from X to Y, i.e. $f: X \to Y$, then

items.quote: The set X is called the domain of the function f.
items.claim: The set X is called the domain of the function f.

items.quote: The set Y is called the codomain of the function f.
items.claim: The set Y is called the codomain of the function f.

items.quote: The set of images of the elements of the domain of X
items.claim: The set of images of the elements of the domain X by the function f is called the range of the function.

items.quote: For example: If f : X → Y
X Y arrow diagram
items.caption: Arrow diagram from X={-1,2,3} to Y={2,3,5,7}: -1→3, 2→7, 3→5.

items.quote: The domain of the function f is the set X = { - 1, 2, 3}
items.text: 1. The domain of the function f is the set $X=\{-1,2,3\}$. 2. The codomain of the function f is the set $Y=\{2,3,5,7\}$. 3. The range of the function f is the set of the images of the elements of X by f and equal to $\{3,5,7\}$.

items.quote: The range is a subset of the codomain of the function.
items.claim: The range is a subset of the codomain of the function.

items.stem: If $X=\{2,3,4\}$, $Y=\{y : y\in N, 2\le y<9\}$ where N is the set of natural numbers, and R is a relation from X to Y where a R b means: « $a=\frac{1}{2}b$ » for each of $a\in X$, $b\in Y$, write R and represent it by an arrow diagram, show that R is a function from X to Y and find its range.
solution: R is a function because every element of the X has only one arrow coming out to one element of Y.
items.notes: Arrow diagram is part of the printed solution (figure k2).

items.caption: Arrow diagram from X to Y. X = {2, 3, 4}; Y = {2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}. Arrows: 2→4, 3→6, 4→8.
items.notes: Arrows read from the figure; verify.

learning_objectives.label: Decide whether a relation is a function
learning_objectives.description: Decide whether a relation from X to Y is a function by checking that each element of X appears only once as a first projection, using arrow diagrams, cartesian diagrams and ordered pairs.

learning_objectives.label: Represent a function symbolically
learning_objectives.description: Write a function with symbols such as f : X → Y, f : x ↦ y and f(x) = y, and name the image of an element.

learning_objectives.label: Represent a function by arrow and cartesian diagrams
learning_objectives.description: Represent a function or relation by a set of ordered pairs, an arrow diagram and a cartesian diagram, and tell which diagrams show functions.

learning_objectives.label: Find the domain, codomain and range of a function
learning_objectives.description: Identify the domain, codomain and range of a function, and see that the range is a subset of the codomain.
